newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen losing steam as blue-chips lag.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen losing steam as blue-chips lag.

text.p: Second-tier stocks led the Warsaw bourse's rebound this week but analysts see their rapid growth leading to equally strong falls, which could pull the market into a fresh round of profit-taking next week.
Analysts said flat or bearish performance of large issues signalled a lack of institutional demand, possibly because funds saw Warsaw blue-chips pricey in comparison with the overall market.
They said small stocks were unlikely to carry the market much further as individual players, who tend to focus on such shares, would be tempted to take quick profits soon after the recent rise.
"No one wants the blue-chips and it's a bad sign as small investors usually come late," said Pawel Hominski, an analyst at DM Magnus brokerage.

Analysts said most of the blue chips, engines of the 30-percent rise since the start of the year, traded at 30 to 40 times earnings, well above the smaller stocks which traded well below the market's average P/E ratio of 16.
They said small issues could extend gains into the next week but saw possible gains lacking sufficient momentum to push the market higher.
The main all-share WIG index inched up 0.9 percent this week to 17,704 and analysts expected 17,000 or 16,500 to provide strong support.
Analysts said deeper correction was unlikely as Poland continued to have strong appeal for foreign investors and any significant falls were likely to spur fresh buying.

Traders expected speculative play on Espebepe, which sent it on a roller-coaster this week, to heat up next week before a meeting of the company's creditors next Friday expected to decide on a possible debt write-off deal.
Espebepe has amassed 80 million zlotys of debts and has said only a deep debt write-off could save it from bankruptcy.
PPABank ends on Monday its second subscription period for 179,271 rights at 15.5 zlotys per share.
The week's top gainers were Prochem, which gained 27.7 percent, Relpol which rose 25 percent and Remak which rose 23.1 percent.
The biggest losers was Elektrim, falling 6.1 percent, Debica, which was down 5.5 percent and Budimex and Bank Slaski, both down 5.4 percent.
